title: Max Consecutive Ones III
summary: You get a list `nums` of 0s and 1s and an integer `k`. You may turn at most k of the 0s into 1s. Return the length of the longest contiguous subarray that holds only 1s after those changes.

examples.explanation: Turn the 0s at indices 4 and 5 into 1s: indices 2 to 8 then hold seven 1s in a row.
No changes are allowed, so the best is the single 1.

approaches.twist: Count the 0s inside the window, and shrink it from the left while it holds more than k of them.
Start from every index and extend to the right until the run would need more than k flips, keeping the longest run.
approaches.note: Works, but starting over from every index takes O(n²) time. The target is O(n).

signals.meaning: The rule is a limit: count the 0s in the window, and shrink it from the left while there are more than k.
The answer is one unbroken stretch. Grow the window to the right and keep the longest length that follows the rule.
Only a 0 can break a run of 1s, so the window's whole state is one number: how many 0s it holds. You never have to choose which 0s to turn.

constraintReading: len(nums) can reach 10⁵, so starting over from every index, O(n²), can take up to 5·10⁹ steps: too slow. Aim for O(n) time and O(1) space: one pass in which each pointer only moves right, keeping a single count of the 0s in the window.

related.relation: Also allows k changes, but the window may end up as any one letter, so it tracks its most common letter instead of its 0s.
